page: Amazon Web Services r8id.96xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 384 vCPUs and 192 physical cores utilizing Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running at 3.9 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It includes 22800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier capabilities in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 1124.8 GB/sec. The hardware supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, which contribute to high-throughput database operations and multi-threaded decompression. In database benchmarks, the instance processed 451.6 million Redis SET operations per second. However, while prompt processing for medium-sized language models performs in the top tier, text generation speeds for smaller models are relatively low, highlighting a performance tradeoff in sequential execution compared to parallelized workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8id.96xlarge offers a high-density resource profile, combining massive DDR5 memory capacity with substantial local NVMe SSD storage on a single instance. This configuration reduces the need for external storage attachments and distributed memory clustering. The instance is suited for memory-intensive and data-heavy workloads, such as large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, high-throughput static web serving, and complex software compilation.
